set.body:
VERIFIED-GOOD, plus a methodological correction against myself.

measurement_form exposes six lowering routes through its route argument: auto, forward_k, pull_h, factorized_h, scalar_stack, multivariate_blocks. These are six different computational strategies for the same quantity, which makes them a natural consistency test - if they are genuinely one operator lowered six ways, they must agree.

THEY AGREE EXACTLY. 12 nodes, 144 edges, 120 features, 8 samples:

  auto                  0.401880805351388
  forward_k             0.401880805351388
  pull_h                0.401880805351388
  factorized_h          0.401880805351388
  scalar_stack          0.401880805351388
  multivariate_blocks   0.401880805351388

  max deviation from auto: 0

Bitwise identical across all six. The correlation view is route-invariant to 5.55e-17, machine epsilon.

This is a strong implementation-level confirmation of the unification claim, complementing the semantic verification on bd-01KZYHGE7SAN8CB8YV4BFJ1CXQ. There the claim was that node effects and coupling are blocks of one operator. Here it is that six independent lowering strategies compute that operator identically. Different axis, same conclusion.

A CORRECTION AGAINST MY OWN FIRST MEASUREMENT, recorded because it is the second time today a naive timing run misled me.

My first pass timed each route once, in a fixed order, and produced:

  auto 1.622 s, forward_k 1.340, pull_h 1.051, factorized_h 1.153,
  scalar_stack 1.042, multivariate_blocks 0.973

which reads as a 1.67x spread with AUTO AS THE SLOWEST ROUTE - a striking result, since an automatic selector choosing the worst of six options would be a real defect worth filing.

It was a warm-up artifact. auto ran first and paid the JIT and allocation costs for everything after it. Re-measured with a discarded warm-up pass, three repetitions per route, and the whole sweep repeated in reverse order:

  route                  fwd order    rev order
  auto                    0.999 s      0.924 s
  forward_k               1.047 s      0.981 s
  pull_h                  0.909 s      0.891 s
  factorized_h            0.948 s      1.059 s
  scalar_stack            1.056 s      1.018 s
  multivariate_blocks     0.951 s      0.955 s

Everything clusters between 0.89 and 1.06 seconds. auto is mid-pack in both orders, and auto/fastest is 1.10x, which is noise. The claim 'auto is slower than every explicit route' is FALSE in both directions.

SO THERE IS NO PERFORMANCE FINDING HERE, and I am not filing one. At this size the route knob does not matter for users, which also means it is reasonable that it is undocumented - unlike the other undocumented capabilities filed today, this one has no user-visible payoff to advertise.

METHOD NOTE, and this is the durable part. This is the second time today that a single-shot timing measurement produced a dramatic and false result. The first was the 40x crossnobis figure on bd-01KZYJXC0NNX4HJ1QJ9BDJKPVZ, which turned out to be 28 separate plan constructions measured against one batched call. Both were caught only by re-measuring under controlled conditions. Anyone doing performance work on this package should discard a warm-up pass, repeat, and reverse the order before believing any ratio - the effects being measured here are smaller than the noise a naive harness introduces.
set.title: Verified: all six lowering routes agree bitwise; the apparent auto-is-slowest result was my own artifact
